name: addition_matrix
display: Addition Matrix: Columns as Rotors, the Law of the Factor Search
summary: The addition matrix of long multiplication read as arithmetic modulo 10^k: columns as rotors, the closed-form law of the digit-by-digit factor search, and the K = 0 address of the final answer.

provenance.origin: Written 2026-10-14 from the Multiplication Matrix Explorer (github.com/michaelrendier/MultiplicationMatrixExplorer), whose matrix_math.py and factor_reconstruction.py this engine reproduces and cross-checks. The Explorer's factor search had measured a x10 growth of live states per digit (2026-09-26); this engine states the count in closed form (units of Z/10^k, valuations of N at 2 and 5), and records that the address of the true factorisation (overflow K = 0) is unique among zero-overflow solutions but not isolated. Prompted by the Collatz parity-shift work (FourthAgePapers/CollatzShift) in which the odometer x -> x + 1 and the maps x -> a x + b on Z/2^n appear.

environment.arithmetic: exact integers; floats only for medians in reports
external: MultiplicationMatrixExplorer (optional: tests/test_addition_matrix.py cross-checks against it when found; set MME_PATH)
